text:
Sarah thought she was a culinary innovator. She wanted her cookies to have a little "kick," so she reached for the chili powder. But in the haze of baking confidence, her hand betrayed her. She grabbed the white powder in the jar next to it, assuming it was salt. It was, in fact, sugar. A lot of it.

The result wasn't spicy. It was a dense, chewy brick of pure, unadulterated sweetness that tasted like someone had melted down a bag of marshmallows and pressed them into a cookie shape.

Her friends took one bite. Their eyes widened. Not in delight, but in sheer, sugary shock. One friend reached for the milk. Then another. Then another. Within minutes, the living room looked like a dairy farm disaster zone. They weren't eating cookies; they were trying to wash down a sugar coma. Sarah stood there, holding the empty jar, realizing she hadn't created a spicy treat, but a lactose-intolerant nightmare. The only thing spicier than the chili powder she *didn't* use was the regret on everyone's faces.
